subject: Alleged missing outputs from API — Novaway (triage & closure)
messages:
From: support@novaway.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Strange truncated outputs from API — examples attached

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing several completions today from the Redwood API where the model output appears truncated mid-sentence. We've attached three examples with request ids and timestamps. The app experienced this between 08:40–09:05 PT; examples include request_id=a3f7c2 and request_id=b8d4e1. The responses sometimes return a 200 with a very short completion (1–2 tokens) and no error.

We've tried replaying once from our side and saw one occurrence, so we're worried it's on your side. Can your team take a look? We rely on streamed completions and this caused a bad UX for a small cohort.

Attachments: novaway_examples_0618.json (application/json) — request/response pairs, timestamps.

Thanks,
Jared Kim
Novaway — Engineering
support@novaway.com

Quick triage update — I ran a replay of the three request payloads from Novaway against the prod endpoint and against a pinned model variant in our staging fleet. No truncations observed in either environment; responses look nominal. I attached the replay log.

Next steps for us and Novaway:
- Novaway: can you share the exact SDK version and any client-side retry/batching settings?
- Novaway: enable verbose logging (sdk.request_id / raw response) for a little while so we can collect a larger sample if it recurs.

Diego — please advise if there are any infra signals I should look at (timeouts, kernel fallbacks), especially around request_id=b8d4e1.

Attachment: api_replay_attempts_0618.log (text)

—Ben

ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange truncated outputs from API — examples attached

I pulled traces and kernel logs for the time window. No host-level OOMs, no autokernel fallback events, and CPU/GPU utilization looks typical. The request routing table shows all three requests routed to our us-west-2 general-purpose pool (model: redwood-13b-v2-int8). I also checked prefix cache hits; nothing suspicious.

Two things to note:
- We see a client-side span with a 1.2s network timeout on one of the request_ids (b8d4e1) before the connection was closed and the SDK retried — that could explain a short response if the client aborted mid-stream.
- There are no server-side logs showing truncation or early stream termination. All server streams that completed have final_chunk markers.

I've uploaded trace snippets and a short runbook note here: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/novaway-traces-0618.

If Novaway can provide the SDK version and any intermediate proxies, that will help. For now I don't see platform evidence to indicate a Redwood-caused truncation.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
SRE, Redwood Inference

We will enable verbose logging for the next 72 hours and send anything new immediately. From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: support@novaway.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange truncated outputs from API — examples attached — closure

Hi Jared — quick closure note from our side after the multi-day triage. TL;DR: we were unable to find platform-side evidence of truncated completions. Replay attempts and prod traces show normal, complete streams for the request_ids you provided. The most likely root cause is client-side/network timeouts leading to socket closes mid-stream.

What we did:
- Replayed customer payloads (see api_replay_attempts_0618.log).
- Checked host/kernel logs and stream termination markers across the routed hosts.
- Examined routing and model variant (redwood-13b-v2-int8) for fallback events.

Findings: no server-side truncation detected; one request shows a client-side network timeout prior to the final_chunk.

Recommendations for Novaway:
- Keep verbose logging enabled for the next 72 hours and share any new request_ids.
- If you see recurrence, include raw request/response pairs plus the SDK version and any proxy/load-balancer in front of the client.
- Consider raising client-side streaming timeouts and ensure your SDK is not aggressively aborting on minor latency spikes.

I've attached a short triage summary for your ticket and linked our internal trace snippets. If the issue returns, we'll reopen the investigation and can schedule a joint debug session. For now we'll close SUP-3921; feel free to re-open.

Attachments: triage_summary_06122.pdf (application/pdf)
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3921

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
